discoveries.brief_text: Has its business model quietly changed, and when?
discoveries.title: Semaglutide, not lenalidomide, is now the swing factor, and it is fragile
discoveries.discovery: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories has already stopped being a North America-led business — North America fell from a 44.9% peak (FY25) to 27.4% of revenue in Q1FY27, below even its FY21 share of 37.8%, while the rest of the business grew 23.5% in FY26 — which makes semaglutide, not lenalidomide, the swing factor, and semaglutide has slipped twice in 8 months, ending in a ₹240 cr write-down (54% of Q1FY27 net profit) and a ~46% cut to the FY27 plan (12 → 6-7 mn pens).
why_it_matters: The lenalidomide cliff is already in the numbers: at 27.4% of revenue, North America is below its FY21 level, so the debate should move from 'how big is the cliff' to 'what replaces it'.
Growth outside North America is broad (Europe +55%, India +16%, Emerging Markets +23%, PSAI +3%, FY26). Part of it was acquired (Agrees to buy Haleon's non-US NRT brands (Nicotinell) for GBP 500m).

Semaglutide is the largest new organic lever, and its setbacks came from different failure points: 30 Oct 2025 (Health Canada): Health Canada notice of non-compliance on semaglutide submission; 9 Jul 2026 (company): Reg-30 filing: semaglutide batches out of specification (API issue).

Its supply chain runs through an external partner (OneSource Specialty Pharma, finished-dose (pen) contract manufacturer; API in-house): a dependency that shows up in partner and press disclosures, not in the segment table.
Sensitivity: the Q1FY27 provision (₹240 cr) equals 54% of that quarter's net profit; the plan cut removes about 5.5 mn pens of supply (midpoint).

evidence_trail.text: FY21 quarterly segment tables (Rs million) Q1-Q4: North America 17,282 + 18,328 + 17,394 + 17,491; Europe 3,551 + 3,754 + 4,143 + 3,956; India 6,260 + 9,123 + 9,591 + 8,445; Emerging Markets 7,982 + 8,636 + 9,623 + 8,845; PSAI 8,553 + 8,505 + 7,009 + 7,915. North America generics business reached Rs. 70.5 billion for the year, up 9% YoY.
evidence_trail.source: Earnings release Q4 FY21

evidence_trail.text: North America: FY25 revenues at Rs 145.2 billion, YoY growth of 12%. The YoY growth was primarily driven by new product launches, increased volumes of select key products, partially offset by price erosion.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's Q4 & Full Year FY25 Financial Results

evidence_trail.text: Revenues 85,452 Mn [Up: 11% YoY; Flat QoQ]. North America 34,123 for Q1FY26, against 38,462 a year earlier ... decline primarily due to increased price erosion in certain key products including Lenalidomide. Europe Rs 12,744 million vs Rs 5,265 million, up 142%, primarily driven by contributions from the acquired NRT portfolio.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's Q1FY26 Financial Results

evidence_trail.text: FY26 Global Generics by region (Rs million): North America 113,737 (down 22%); Emerging Markets 67,608 (up 23%); India 62,186 (up 16%); Europe 55,501 (up 55%). PSAI 34,774 (up 3%). Revenue Rs 335.9 billion, up 3.2%.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's Q4 & Full Year FY26 Financial Results (6-K Ex 99.2)

evidence_trail.text: Certain batches of semaglutide were found to be out of specification due to an issue associated with the API ... the company is investigating the root cause ... commercial supplies of the product will be delayed for a certain period of time. The issue has no impact on patient safety and does not affect the product's existing global regulatory filings.
evidence_trail.source: Intimation to NSE/BSE/NYSE: semaglutide supply delay (6-K Ex 99.1)

evidence_trail.text: Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026): revenue Rs 80,705 million, down 5.6% YoY. Emerging Markets Rs 18,328 million (up 31%); India Rs 17,177 million (up 17%); Europe Rs 14,440 million (up 13%); PSAI about Rs 852 crore (up about 4%).
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's Q1 FY27 results (6-K Ex 99.2)

evidence_trail.text: A provision of Rs.2,397 million towards inventory and other associated costs, as certain batches of semaglutide were found to be out of specification due to an issue associated with the API.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's Q1 FY27 results (6-K Ex 99.2)

evidence_trail.text: OneSource said its partner Dr. Reddy's received Health Canada authorization for a generic semaglutide injection; OneSource acts as the contract manufacturer, handling scale-up and commercial production at its US FDA-approved facility in Bengaluru.
evidence_trail.source: OneSource's partner Dr. Reddy's receives Health Canada approval for Semaglutide Injection

evidence_trail.text: Health Canada's Pharmaceutical Drugs Directorate issued a notice of non-compliance on the company's abbreviated new drug submission for semaglutide; analysts estimated a delay of at least eight to 12 months; the stock fell more than 4%.
evidence_trail.source: Canada notice may delay Dr Reddy's semaglutide generic launch

evidence_trail.text: The active ingredient is made entirely in-house, while the finished product is currently manufactured in collaboration with OneSource.
evidence_trail.source: OneSource Pharma, Dr Reddy's secure Health Canada nod for generic Semaglutide

evidence_trail.text: Dr. Reddy's is described as OneSource's anchor customer.
evidence_trail.source: OneSource Specialty Pharma stock: what the FY28 bet rests on

evidence_trail.text: Dr Reddy's delays semaglutide supply due to API issue; shares slide. NSE-listed shares dropped as much as 6.5% to 1,261.10 rupees.
evidence_trail.source: Dr Reddy's delays semaglutide supply due to API issue; shares slide

evidence_trail.text: The FY27 supply target was cut to 6-7 million pens from 12 million; API testing completion targeted by the third week of September 2026 and commercial supply resumption in November; management put the probability of delivering 6-7 million pens between November and March at 80-90%.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's Q1 FY27 slides show base growth amid semaglutide hit

evidence_trail.text: Revenue from the North America business fell 35.38% YoY to Rs 2,204.8 crore, mainly due to lower sales of Lenalidomide. Net profit plunged 69% YoY to Rs 444 crore.
evidence_trail.source: Dr Reddys Labs slides after Q1 PAT plunges 69% YoY to Rs 444 crore

evidence_trail.text: Management called the quarter an expected transition away from lenalidomide revenue ... Its underlying base business continued to deliver healthy double-digit growth across all key geographies.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's Q1 FY27 slides show base growth amid semaglutide hit

evidence_trail.text: The fix is process remediation and does not require regulatory re-approvals; API supply to OneSource to resume by October 2026.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's Expects Strong Q3 And Q4 Performance After Fixing Semaglutide Problems

evidence_trail.text: An out-of-specification degradation impurity appeared during scale-up; the API itself met specifications and the impurity formed in the finished formulation.
evidence_trail.source: Semaglutide Update - Dr. Reddy's Laboratories

evidence_trail.text: Management indicated that demand from other customers and markets was sufficient to absorb the available capacity.
evidence_trail.source: OneSource Specialty Pharma: Q1FY27 May Have Been the Proof of Concept

evidence_trail.text: Q4 FY26: consolidated revenue Rs 75,162 million, down 11.6% YoY. North America fell 51% to Rs 17,562 million; Emerging Markets up 29%, India up 20%, Europe up 14%. Excluding the Rs 4.5 billion shelf stock adjustment, FY26 revenue about Rs 340.5 billion.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's Q4 & Full Year FY26 Financial Results (6-K Ex 99.2)

evidence_trail.text: North America ... declined 22% for the full year ... largely due to lower Lenalidomide sales and a one-time shelf stock adjustment related to the product.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's Q4 & Full Year FY26 Financial Results (6-K Ex 99.2)

evidence_trail.text: Dr. Reddy's announced the launch of its generic semaglutide injection in Canada following a Notice of Compliance from Health Canada dated April 28, 2026.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's press release: generic semaglutide launch in Canada (6-K Ex 99.1)

evidence_trail.text: Dr. Reddy's agreed to buy Haleon's non-US NRT brands, including Nicotinell, through a Swiss holding company, Northstar Switzerland SARL, for GBP 500 million (GBP 458 million upfront, up to GBP 42 million performance-based).
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's to acquire Nicotinell from Haleon

evidence_trail.text: After Lenalidomide, Dr Reddy's turns to obesity drugs, biosimilars and consumer health.
evidence_trail.source: After Lenalidomide, Dr Reddy's turns to obesity drugs, biosimilars and consumer health

evidence_trail.text: Dr. Reddy's is also licensed to sell generic lenalidomide capsules in the U.S. without volume limitation beginning on January 31, 2026.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's announces the launch of Lenalidomide Capsules in the U.S.

evidence_trail.text: Sun Pharma US formulation sales fell 9.7% to $427 million in Q1 FY27.
evidence_trail.source: Sun Pharmaceutical Q1 FY27 result: US formulation sales decline to $427 million

evidence_trail.text: Cipla North America business was down 28 per cent year over year in Q1 FY27.
evidence_trail.source: Cipla's Q1 net falls 39% on US business; maintains FY27 margin guidance

evidence_trail.text: The acquired NRT portfolio generated about GBP 217 million in revenue in CY23.
evidence_trail.source: Dr. Reddy's to acquire nicotine replacement brands from UK-based Haleon for $632 m
